strings.name: John Kerry
strings.role: Diplomat · former US secretary of state and climate envoy
strings.summary: A Yale graduate and Vietnam veteran, Kerry became an antiwar advocate before entering Massachusetts and federal politics. He represented the state in the Senate from 1985 to 2013 and was the 2004 Democratic presidential nominee. As secretary of state he participated in Iran nuclear and Paris climate negotiations, then served as presidential climate envoy from 2021 to 2024. These agreements were multilateral achievements; he continued climate advocacy after office.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A former US secretary of state who participated in the Iran nuclear negotiations and Paris Agreement and has long worked in international climate diplomacy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated from Yale in 1966 and later earned a law degree at Boston College.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Multilateral negotiations
strings.highlights.h1.text: As secretary of state participated in negotiations for the 2015 Iran nuclear deal and Paris Agreement.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Climate envoy work
strings.highlights.h2.text: Conducted international climate diplomacy as special presidential envoy from 2021 to 2024.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Left climate envoy post
strings.timeline.t1.text: Ended his government envoy term, continuing climate advocacy and public-policy discussion afterward.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became presidential climate envoy
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became the first US special presidential envoy for climate, focused on international diplomacy.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Signed Paris Agreement for the US
strings.timeline.t3.text: Represented the US at UN headquarters in signing the multilateral agreement reached in 2015.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Helped negotiate Iran nuclear deal
strings.timeline.t4.text: As secretary of state joined the multinational negotiations producing the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became secretary of state
strings.timeline.t5.text: Moved from the Senate to Obama’s cabinet, serving until 2017.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Ran for president
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the Democratic nomination but lost the general election to incumbent George W. Bush.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered US Senate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began representing Massachusetts, later chairing the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Testified as a Vietnam veteran
strings.timeline.t8.text: Testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and became a prominent antiwar voice.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Graduated from Yale and enlisted
strings.timeline.t9.text: Enlisted in the Naval Reserve shortly before graduating from Yale, continuing into service in Vietnam.
